adverse_media.summary: Financial Times reported inconsistencies in Wirecard's accounting
Short-seller research (Zatarra) alleged fraudulent activity and money laundering by senior executives
Southern Investigative Reporting Foundation concluded that at least €175m of the €340m paid for Wirecard's 2015 acquisition of an India-based payment processor was not transferred to the seller

FT reported whistleblower allegations that Wirecard's Asia-Pacific head of accounting (Edo Kurniawan) forged and backdated contracts to inflate profit; Singapore authorities raided Wirecard offices in February 2019
BaFin imposed a short-selling ban following press reports on wrongdoing at Wirecard
BaFin fined Wirecard AG (€1.52m, announced by the Federal Ministry of Finance 16.07.2020) for failure to appropriately disclose financial reports on time

Munich prosecutors searched Wirecard HQ and opened proceedings against the entire management board in a BaFin-initiated market-manipulation probe over possibly misleading statements (12 March – 22 April period); Wirecard denied the allegations; BaFin also probed CEO Braun for insider trading
KPMG special audit found insufficient documentation to address allegations of accounting irregularities; could not confirm the €1.9bn escrow balance
EY refused to sign off the 2019 accounts, unable to confirm €1.9bn in cash balances; on 22 June Wirecard admitted the €1.9bn bank trust account balances probably never existed
CEO Markus Braun arrested on suspicion of falsifying accounts (23 June); company filed for insolvency on 25 June 2020 owing creditors almost $4 billion
Raids on Wirecard HQ; prosecutors investigated suspected money laundering; head of the Dubai-based subsidiary arrested 6 July and admitted wrongdoing on 16 July

adverse_media.status: opened; liquidation ongoing (7th status report covering Dec 2023 – May 2024)
adverse_media.summary: Insolvency proceedings opened over Wirecard AG's assets by Amtsgericht München (Az. 1542 IN 1308/20) on grounds of insolvency and over-indebtedness; company dissolved by operation of law (§263 AktG); administrator Dr. Michael Jaffé appointed

adverse_media.status: trial ongoing (still running as of Nov 2025 after 230+ hearing days)
adverse_media.summary: German prosecutors filed the first charges in the Wirecard fraud; trial of former CEO Markus Braun, Oliver Bellenhaus (ex-head of the Dubai subsidiary) and Stephan von Erffa (ex-head of accounting) opened at Munich I Regional Court for what is described as the biggest fraud case in German history
Singapore State Court sentenced Wirecard international finance manager James Wardhana to 21 months and Wirecard Asia head of finance Chai Ai Lim to 10 months imprisonment
adverse_media.category: criminal conviction of group finance staff

adverse_media.status: ongoing; Marsalek at large (Europol/Interpol wanted, per European Parliament question of 2025)
adverse_media.summary: BR investigation: the €1.9bn third-party acquirer balances never existed; about €2bn flowed into alleged third-party acquirer accounts at Wirecard Bank, with multi-million transfers from shell companies linked to illegal gambling and identified by BR as substantially owned by Calvin Ayre; former COO Jan Marsalek remains a fugitive (Europol most-wanted, Interpol wanted, reported stays in Belarus/Russia/UAE)
adverse_media.category: money laundering / fraud (ongoing investigation and reporting)

output.risk_rationale: HIGH. Registration: Wirecard AG (HRB 169227, Amtsgericht München) was dissolved by operation of law when insolvency proceedings were opened on 25.08.2020 (AG München, Az. 1542 IN 1308/20) and is now in liquidation; its LEI 529900A8LX4KL0YUTH71 has been LAPSED since 2020-11-13. Adverse media over the last 10 years is exceptional: the confirmed €1.9 billion accounting fraud (2020), a ~$4bn insolvency, the criminal trial of former CEO Markus Braun and two other former executives (ongoing since Dec 2022, still running Nov 2025), money-laundering probes of Wirecard Bank flows linked to illegal gambling, enforcement actions by BaFin (fines, short-selling ban), and convictions of Wirecard finance staff in Singapore. Former COO Jan Marsalek is a fugitive wanted by Interpol/Europol. Sanctions screening of the entity and its leadership found no match on the UK Sanctions List (verified directly against the official CSV of 03-Nov-2026), and no matches were identified for OFAC SDN or the EU consolidated list (both screened 2026-11-09; direct OFAC list file download timed out, so that negative is based on portal/press review). No PEP matches were identified among directors or beneficial owners. The entity itself is defunct, which is terminal rather than an ongoing trading risk, but for screening history purposes the fraud, insolvency and money-laundering record mandate a HIGH risk rating.
